Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১) Fatty change of heart may occur in......?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fatty change of the myocardium can occur in diphtheria, primarily due to the cardiotoxic effect of diphtheria toxin. The toxin inhibits protein synthesis by inactivating elongation factor-2, leading to cellular injury. Diphtheritic myocarditis may develop during the acute illness and can cause myocardial degeneration, including fatty change, myocardial necrosis, conduction abnormalities, and potentially fatal arrhythmias or heart failure. TB and syphilis can involve the heart, but fatty myocardial degeneration is not a characteristic finding. Measles is also not classically associated with fatty change of the heart.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Diphtheria toxin → myocardial injury

  • Diphtheria may cause myocarditis and conduction defects.

  • Fatty degeneration can occur in organs subjected to toxic/metabolic injury.

  • Severe diphtheritic myocarditis can cause arrhythmias and heart failure.

Exam Pearl:
Diphtheria is a classic cause of toxic myocarditis with fatty degeneration of the myocardium.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২) Which is the 1st relay station of pain?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The first relay station for pain sensation is the spinal cord, particularly the dorsal horn of the spinal cord. Primary nociceptive afferent fibers enter through the dorsal roots and synapse mainly in the substantia gelatinosa and other dorsal horn laminae. The second-order neurons then cross to the opposite side and ascend mainly in the spinothalamic tract toward the thalamus. The thalamus is therefore a major higher relay station, but it is not the first relay station for pain. Pons and medulla are involved in pain modulation and descending control but are not the primary first relay.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • 1st-order neuron: Dorsal root ganglion

  • First synapse/relay: Dorsal horn of spinal cord

  • Major ascending pathway: Spinothalamic tract

  • Major supraspinal relay: Thalamus

  • Pain fibers mainly use A-delta and C fibers

Exam Pearl:
For pain, the first relay is the spinal dorsal horn; the thalamus is the major higher relay.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩) Which is not a feature of metastatic calcification?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Metastatic calcification is the deposition of calcium salts in otherwise normal tissues, usually due to hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia. Common sites include the kidneys, lungs, gastric mucosa, and systemic arteries. Nephrocalcinosis is a classic manifestation because calcium deposition can occur in the renal interstitium and tubules. In contrast, psammoma bodies are microscopic, concentrically laminated calcifications that occur in certain tumors, such as papillary thyroid carcinoma, serous papillary tumors of the ovary, and meningioma. They represent dystrophic calcification, which occurs in damaged or necrotic tissue and generally does not require hypercalcemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Metastatic calcification → normal tissue

  • Usually associated with hypercalcemia

  • Common sites: kidneys, lungs, gastric mucosa, arteries

  • Nephrocalcinosis → metastatic calcification

  • Psammoma bodies → dystrophic calcification

Exam Pearl:
Psammoma body = dystrophic calcification, not metastatic calcification.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪) In Brown Sequard syndrome which sensation is lost on same side?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Brown-Séquard syndrome results from hemisection of the spinal cord. The dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway, which carries proprioception, vibration, and fine/discriminative touch, ascends ipsilaterally in the spinal cord and crosses in the medulla. Therefore, a spinal cord hemisection causes ipsilateral loss of proprioception below the level of the lesion. In contrast, pain and temperature fibers in the spinothalamic tract cross within the spinal cord, usually within 1–2 segments after entering, producing contralateral loss of pain and temperature below the lesion. Touch may be variably affected because it has contributions from multiple pathways.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ipsilateral: Proprioception, vibration, fine touch

  • Contralateral: Pain and temperature

  • Dorsal columns cross in the medulla

  • Spinothalamic fibers cross in the spinal cord

  • Brown-Séquard = hemisection of spinal cord

Exam Pearl:
Brown-Séquard: same side loses proprioception; opposite side loses pain and temperature.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫) Which is wear and tear pigment?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Lipofuscin is known as the “wear-and-tear pigment” because it accumulates progressively in long-lived cells as a result of oxidative damage and incomplete degradation of cellular components, particularly membrane lipids. It is commonly seen in cardiac myocytes, hepatocytes, and neurons, especially with aging. Lipofuscin appears as a fine, yellow-brown, granular cytoplasmic pigment. Melanin is responsible for pigmentation of the skin and other tissues, hemosiderin represents stored iron, and coal dust (carbon) accumulates in the lungs and lymph nodes as an exogenous pigment. Lipofuscin accumulation in the heart may contribute to the characteristic brown atrophy of the heart seen with aging or chronic wasting.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Lipofuscin = wear-and-tear pigment

  • Derived from lipid peroxidation and residual bodies

  • Common in heart, liver, and neurons

  • Brown atrophy of heart → lipofuscin

  • Hemosiderin = iron-storage pigment

  • Melanin = endogenous brown-black pigment

Exam Pearl:
Lipofuscin = “wear-and-tear” pigment of aging cells.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬) End plate potential is characterized by….?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The end-plate potential (EPP) is the local depolarization that occurs at the motor end plate of skeletal muscle following release of acetylcholine (ACh) from the presynaptic motor nerve terminal. ACh binds to nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (Nm) on the postsynaptic membrane, opening ligand-gated cation channels. This produces a net inward movement of positive ions, mainly Na⁺, causing local depolarization of the end plate. If the EPP reaches threshold, it activates nearby voltage-gated Na⁺ channels and generates a propagated muscle action potential. Unlike an action potential, the EPP is a graded potential and does not undergo an all-or-none response.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • EPP = depolarization of motor end plate

  • Neurotransmitter: Acetylcholine

  • Receptor: Nicotinic Nm receptor

  • EPP is a graded potential

  • Muscle action potential is all-or-none

  • EPP itself does not propagate along the entire muscle membrane

Exam Pearl:
End-plate potential is a graded depolarization produced by ACh at the neuromuscular junction.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭) Hypertrophy occurs in... Cells?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual cells, resulting in enlargement of the affected organ or tissue. It is particularly characteristic of stable cells, which have limited proliferative capacity but can increase their functional capacity and cellular mass in response to increased workload. A classic example is cardiac muscle hypertrophy in response to chronic hypertension. Permanent cells, such as cardiac myocytes and skeletal muscle fibers, can also undergo hypertrophy, so the question is somewhat simplified. Labile cells primarily respond to increased demand through hyperplasia, because they are capable of continuous proliferation. Therefore, among the given options, stable cells is the best conventional exam answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypertrophy → increased cell size

  • Hyperplasia → increased cell number

  • Stable cells have limited proliferative capacity.

  • Cardiac myocytes respond to increased workload mainly by hypertrophy.

  • Labile cells commonly undergo hyperplasia.

Exam Pearl:
For a single-best-answer exam, “Stable cells” is the best choice for hypertrophy, although permanent cells can also hypertrophy.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮) Which is best for increasing muscle strength?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Isometric exercise involves contraction of a muscle without a significant change in its length or movement of the joint. It is particularly effective for improving muscle strength, especially at or near the specific joint angle at which the exercise is performed. It is useful when joint movement is painful or contraindicated, such as during early rehabilitation. Isotonic exercise involves muscle shortening or lengthening with movement and is excellent for improving strength, endurance, and functional performance, but in this classic exam question, isometric exercise is the preferred answer for increasing muscle strength. “Atonic exercise” is not a standard exercise category, while electrical stimulation may assist muscle activation but is not the best general method for strength training.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Isometric → tension increases, muscle length remains relatively constant

  • Isometric training improves muscle strength

  • Strength gains are greatest near the trained joint angle.

  • Isotonic → muscle length changes with joint movement

  • Electrical stimulation can be used for muscle re-education/rehabilitation.

Exam Pearl:
For classic MCQs asking the best exercise to increase muscle strength, choose isometric exercise.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯) Where squamous metaplasia doesn't occur?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Barrett’s esophagus is characterized by intestinal metaplasia, in which the normal stratified squamous epithelium of the distal esophagus is replaced by columnar epithelium containing goblet cells, usually due to chronic gastroesophageal reflux. Therefore, it is not an example of squamous metaplasia. In contrast, sialolithiasis can cause chronic irritation of salivary ducts and may lead to squamous metaplasia. Vitamin A deficiency can cause squamous metaplasia of respiratory and other epithelia. Chronic cigarette smoking is a classic cause of squamous metaplasia of the bronchial epithelium, with replacement of normal ciliated columnar epithelium by stratified squamous epithelium.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Barrett’s esophagus → intestinal/columnar metaplasia

  • Chronic smoking → squamous metaplasia of bronchial epithelium

  • Vitamin A deficiency → squamous metaplasia

  • Chronic irritation in salivary ducts → may cause squamous metaplasia

  • Metaplasia is generally reversible if the stimulus is removed.

Exam Pearl:
Barrett’s esophagus = columnar intestinal metaplasia, not squamous metaplasia.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০) Itching is caused by stimulation of which nerve fiber?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Explanation:
Itch (pruritus) is primarily transmitted by specialized unmyelinated C fibers, particularly slow-conducting C-type afferents. These fibers are distributed in the superficial layers of the skin and respond to pruritogenic stimuli such as histamine and other inflammatory mediators. Their impulses enter the dorsal horn of the spinal cord and are transmitted mainly through ascending spinothalamic pathways to higher centers. C fibers also carry slow pain, whereas A-delta fibers mainly transmit fast, sharp pain. B fibers are primarily preganglionic autonomic fibers and are not the principal fibers responsible for itch.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Itch → C fibers

  • C fibers are unmyelinated and slow-conducting

  • C fibers also carry slow pain

  • A-delta fibers → fast, sharp pain

  • B fibers → preganglionic autonomic fibers

Exam Pearl:
Itch is mainly transmitted by unmyelinated C fibers.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১১) 'Smudgy pink appearance in vascular wall' is morphological feature of........ Necrosis?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fibrinoid necrosis is characterized microscopically by a smudgy, intensely eosinophilic (pink) appearance within the walls of blood vessels. It results from severe vascular injury with deposition of fibrin, plasma proteins, and immune complexes in the vessel wall. It is classically seen in immune-mediated vasculitis, malignant hypertension, and some immune-related vascular lesions. Caseous necrosis produces a cheese-like, granular appearance, typically associated with tuberculosis. Fat necrosis involves destruction of adipose tissue with fatty acid release and calcium soap formation (saponification). Gangrenous necrosis is a clinical pattern, usually involving ischemic tissue, and may be dry or complicated by infection.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Fibrinoid necrosis → vascular wall

  • Microscopy → smudgy, bright eosinophilic/pink material

  • Seen in vasculitis

  • Also associated with malignant hypertension

  • Caseous → cheese-like appearance

  • Fat necrosis → saponification

Exam Pearl:
Smudgy pink/eosinophilic material in a blood vessel wall = fibrinoid necrosis.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১২) Which one controls circadian rhythm?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of the hypothalamus is the principal biological clock that controls the circadian rhythm. It receives direct input from the retina through the retinohypothalamic tract, allowing the light–dark cycle to synchronize the body's internal clock. The SCN regulates sleep–wake cycles and influences daily rhythms in hormone secretion, body temperature, and autonomic activity. The pineal gland contributes to circadian regulation by secreting melatonin under SCN control. The raphe nuclei are primarily involved in serotonin-mediated functions, while the red nucleus is involved in motor coordination. The paraventricular nucleus has important neuroendocrine and autonomic functions but is not the principal circadian pacemaker.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • SCN → master circadian clock

  • Located in the anterior hypothalamus

  • Receives light information from the retina via the retinohypothalamic tract

  • SCN regulates melatonin secretion through the pineal gland

  • Melatonin promotes synchronization of the sleep–wake cycle

Exam Pearl:
Suprachiasmatic nucleus = master biological clock controlling circadian rhythm.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৩) Which one is corresponding receptor on leukocytes for collections?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The question likely refers to the leukocyte receptor involved in collection/adhesion of complement-opsonized particles. CR3 (CD11b/CD18) is an integrin receptor expressed on neutrophils, monocytes, and macrophages. It binds iC3b, an important complement-derived opsonin, and facilitates the adhesion and phagocytosis of opsonized microorganisms and immune complexes. CR1 (CD35) also binds complement fragments, particularly C3b and C4b, and has important immune-complex clearance functions. CR2 (CD21) is mainly expressed on B cells and follicular dendritic cells. C1q is a complement component rather than a leukocyte receptor. Therefore, among these options, CR3 is the best answer for leukocyte-mediated collection/phagocytosis of complement-opsonized material.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CR3 (CD11b/CD18) → binds iC3b

  • CR3 is important for phagocytosis and adhesion

  • CR1 (CD35) → C3b/C4b

  • CR2 (CD21) → B cells; binds C3d

  • C1q → complement component, not a leukocyte receptor

Exam Pearl:
CR3 on leukocytes binds iC3b and promotes phagocytosis of opsonized particles.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৪) Interneurons are not functioning in which reflex?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The stretch (myotatic) reflex is a classic monosynaptic reflex, meaning the sensory afferent from the muscle spindle forms a direct excitatory synapse with the alpha motor neuron in the spinal cord. Therefore, no interneuron is required for the essential reflex arc. In contrast, the withdrawal reflex is polysynaptic and requires interneurons to coordinate flexor activation and extensor inhibition. Swallowing is a complex brainstem-mediated reflex involving multiple interneuronal circuits, while visual reflexes also involve interneurons within central neural pathways. Thus, the stretch reflex is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Stretch reflex → monosynaptic

  • Receptor → muscle spindle

  • Afferent fiber → Ia

  • Efferent neuron → alpha motor neuron

  • No interneuron in the basic stretch reflex arc

  • Withdrawal reflex → polysynaptic

Exam Pearl:
Stretch reflex = simplest monosynaptic reflex = no interneuron.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৫) Which is plasma protein derived chemical mediator of inflammation?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Complement proteins are plasma protein-derived chemical mediators of inflammation. They circulate in the blood mainly as inactive precursors and become activated through the classical, alternative, or lectin pathways. Complement activation produces biologically active fragments such as C3a and C5a, which promote inflammation. C5a is a particularly potent chemotactic agent and also activates leukocytes, while C3a and C5a contribute to increased vascular permeability through mast-cell activation. Cytokines and chemokines are primarily produced by activated cells, including macrophages, endothelial cells, and lymphocytes. Caspases are intracellular proteolytic enzymes involved mainly in apoptosis and inflammasome-related processes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Complement → plasma-derived mediator

  • C3a, C5a → anaphylatoxins

  • C5a → powerful chemotactic factor

  • C3b → opsonization

  • Cytokines/chemokines → mainly cell-derived mediators

  • Caspases → intracellular proteases

Exam Pearl:
Among the options, complement is the classic plasma protein-derived mediator of inflammation.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৬) Prolactin inhibiting hormone is…..in nature?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Dopamine is the principal prolactin-inhibiting hormone (prolactin-inhibiting factor) released from the hypothalamus. It travels through the hypothalamic–hypophyseal portal circulation to the anterior pituitary, where it acts on D2 receptors on lactotroph cells and suppresses prolactin synthesis and secretion. This is somewhat unusual because most hypothalamic hormones stimulate anterior pituitary secretion, whereas dopamine provides predominantly tonic inhibition of prolactin release. Interruption of hypothalamic dopamine delivery, such as from a pituitary stalk lesion, therefore causes hyperprolactinemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Dopamine → prolactin-inhibiting factor

  • Acts through D2 receptors on lactotrophs

  • Dopamine provides tonic inhibition of prolactin secretion.

  • Pituitary stalk interruption → increased prolactin

  • Prolactin secretion increases when hypothalamic dopamine inhibition decreases.

Exam Pearl:
Dopamine is the major physiological inhibitor of prolactin secretion.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৭) Which is the most prominent manifestation of acute phase response?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fever is the most prominent and characteristic systemic manifestation of the acute-phase response. Acute inflammation stimulates the release of endogenous pyrogens, particularly IL-1, IL-6, and TNF, from activated macrophages and other cells. These cytokines act on the hypothalamus, increasing prostaglandin E₂ (PGE₂) production and raising the hypothalamic temperature set point, resulting in fever. The acute-phase response also produces nonspecific symptoms such as malaise, anorexia, and fatigue, but these are less characteristic than fever. IL-6 is particularly important in stimulating hepatic synthesis of acute-phase proteins such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and fibrinogen.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Fever → prominent systemic manifestation of acute inflammation

  • Major endogenous pyrogens: IL-1, IL-6, TNF

  • Hypothalamic mediator: PGE₂

  • IL-6 → hepatic acute-phase protein synthesis

  • CRP and fibrinogen are important acute-phase proteins.

Exam Pearl:
Acute-phase response: think fever + IL-6 + CRP.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৮) Beta endorphins are highly found in…..?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
β-Endorphin is an endogenous opioid peptide derived from proopiomelanocortin (POMC) and contributes to endogenous pain modulation. In the spinal cord, opioid peptides are particularly abundant in the substantia gelatinosa (lamina II) of the dorsal horn, where they modulate nociceptive transmission. Activation of opioid receptors can inhibit neurotransmitter release from primary afferent nociceptors and reduce postsynaptic neuronal excitability, thereby suppressing pain transmission. Although β-endorphin is also present in the hypothalamus and released into the circulation from the anterior pituitary, among the given options, substantia gelatinosa is the best answer in the context of spinal pain modulation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Substantia gelatinosa → major site of spinal pain modulation

  • Contains endogenous opioids including enkephalins and endorphins

  • Located in lamina II of the dorsal horn

  • Opioids inhibit nociceptive neurotransmission.

  • β-Endorphin is derived from POMC.

Exam Pearl:
Substantia gelatinosa is the key spinal site for endogenous opioid-mediated pain inhibition.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৯) Oedema due to hypoproteinemia occurs in.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypoproteinemic edema occurs when plasma protein, particularly albumin, falls, causing a reduction in plasma colloid oncotic pressure. This favors movement of fluid from the intravascular compartment into the interstitial space, producing edema. Liver cirrhosis is a classic cause because impaired hepatic synthesis of albumin leads to hypoalbuminemia. Cirrhosis may also cause portal hypertension, further contributing to fluid accumulation and ascites. Left heart failure primarily causes increased hydrostatic pressure, while hypothyroidism causes myxedema due largely to accumulation of glycosaminoglycans rather than simple hypoalbuminemia. Radiation therapy is not a typical cause of generalized hypoproteinemic edema.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypoproteinemia → decreased plasma oncotic pressure

  • Major protein involved: Albumin

  • Cirrhosis → reduced albumin synthesis

  • Nephrotic syndrome → urinary protein loss

  • Protein-losing enteropathy → GI protein loss

  • Heart failure → mainly increased hydrostatic pressure

Exam Pearl:
Cirrhosis causes edema primarily through hypoalbuminemia and reduced plasma oncotic pressure.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২০) Which one has shortest half-life in plasma?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Acetylcholine (ACh) has an extremely short duration of action because it is rapidly hydrolyzed by acetylcholinesterase into acetate and choline. Its effective half-life at cholinergic synapses is only milliseconds, making it much shorter-lived than epinephrine, dopamine, or prolactin. Epinephrine and dopamine are metabolized primarily by COMT and MAO and have plasma half-lives of roughly a few minutes, while prolactin has a substantially longer half-life. Strictly speaking, ACh is not normally considered a circulating plasma hormone, so the wording “half-life in plasma” is imperfect; however, among the given options, ACh is clearly the shortest-lived substance.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acetylcholine → half-life in milliseconds

  • Rapidly degraded by acetylcholinesterase

  • Epinephrine → plasma half-life approximately 1–3 minutes

  • Dopamine → plasma half-life approximately 1–2 minutes

  • Prolactin → half-life approximately 20–30 minutes

Exam Pearl:
Acetylcholine is the shortest-lived neurotransmitter here because acetylcholinesterase destroys it almost immediately.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২১) Pathological condition caused by vascular congestion excludes.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Chocolate cyst of the ovary is an endometriotic cyst formed by ectopic endometrial tissue within the ovary. Repeated cyclical bleeding into the cyst leads to accumulation of old, altered blood, giving it its characteristic “chocolate” appearance. It is not a consequence of vascular congestion. In contrast, nutmeg liver results from chronic passive venous congestion of the liver, usually due to right-sided heart failure. Brown induration of the lung is caused by chronic pulmonary venous congestion, commonly due to left-sided heart failure, with hemosiderin accumulation in macrophages. Stasis dermatitis of the leg results from chronic venous insufficiency and venous congestion, causing edema, hemosiderin deposition, and skin changes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nutmeg liver → chronic hepatic venous congestion

  • Brown induration of lung → chronic pulmonary congestion

  • Stasis dermatitis → chronic venous congestion

  • Chocolate cyst → ovarian endometriosis

  • Chronic congestion may cause edema and hemosiderin deposition.

Exam Pearl:
Chocolate cyst = endometriosis, not vascular congestion.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২২) What is the half life of transfused platelet?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The normal lifespan of circulating platelets is approximately 7–10 days, but the effective survival of transfused platelets is shorter, commonly around 3–5 days depending on storage conditions, recipient factors, and platelet quality. Therefore, among the given options, 4 days is the best answer. Transfused platelets are removed from circulation by the reticuloendothelial system, particularly the spleen, as they age or become functionally altered. In clinical practice, platelet transfusion is generally used to provide temporary hemostatic support, especially in thrombocytopenia or platelet dysfunction.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Normal platelet lifespan: approximately 7–10 days

  • Transfused platelet survival: approximately 3–5 days

  • Best option here: 4 days

  • Platelets are primarily cleared by the reticuloendothelial system

  • Spleen plays an important role in platelet sequestration and removal.

Exam Pearl:
Transfused platelet survival is about 4 days; normal platelet lifespan is about 7–10 days.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৩) Septic shock results from following except....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Septic shock is a life-threatening form of circulatory failure caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. It most commonly arises from severe infections involving the lungs, abdomen, urinary tract, or bloodstream. Pneumonia is a major source of sepsis and septic shock, while peritonitis can produce severe intra-abdominal sepsis. Osteomyelitis, particularly when severe or associated with bacteremia, can also lead to sepsis and septic shock. Keratitis is generally a localized infection of the cornea and is much less likely to produce systemic sepsis or septic shock. Therefore, among the given options, keratitis is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Common sources of septic shock: lung, abdomen, urinary tract, bloodstream

  • Pneumonia → major cause of sepsis

  • Peritonitis → important cause of intra-abdominal sepsis

  • Osteomyelitis → can cause bacteremia and sepsis

  • Keratitis → usually localized ocular infection

Exam Pearl:
Among these options, keratitis is least likely to cause septic shock.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৪) Glycophorin is seen in.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Glycophorin is a major sialoglycoprotein of the erythrocyte membrane. Glycophorin A is particularly abundant on red blood cells and contains a high proportion of sialic acid, which contributes to the negative surface charge of erythrocytes and helps prevent them from adhering to one another. It also serves as an important membrane antigen and is involved in blood group antigen expression. Glycophorin A is used as a marker of erythroid differentiation. The other listed cells—enterocytes, hepatocytes, and lymphocytes—do not characteristically express glycophorin as a major membrane glycoprotein.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Glycophorin → erythrocyte membrane

  • Glycophorin A is the major form.

  • Rich in sialic acid

  • Gives RBCs a negative surface charge

  • Important in erythroid cell identification and blood group antigen expression

Exam Pearl:
Glycophorin = characteristic membrane glycoprotein of red blood cells.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৫) Which is not benign tumor histologically?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Medulloblastoma is a malignant embryonal tumor of the central nervous system, typically arising in the cerebellum, especially in children. Histologically, it is characterized by densely packed, primitive small cells with scant cytoplasm and a high mitotic rate. In contrast, meningioma and schwannoma are generally benign CNS-associated tumors, although rare atypical or malignant variants exist. Craniopharyngioma is also generally considered a benign, slow-growing epithelial tumor arising in the sellar/suprasellar region, despite its potential for local invasion and significant clinical morbidity. Therefore, among the given options, medulloblastoma is the clear malignant tumor.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Medulloblastoma → malignant embryonal tumor

  • Common location → cerebellum

  • Predominantly occurs in children

  • Meningioma → usually benign

  • Schwannoma → usually benign

  • Craniopharyngioma → generally benign but locally aggressive

Exam Pearl:
Medulloblastoma is the malignant tumor among these options.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৬) For which affect the affinity of oxygen for Hb increases with fall in pH?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The Bohr effect describes the reduction in hemoglobin’s affinity for oxygen when pH falls or CO₂ rises. In metabolically active tissues, increased CO₂ production and H⁺ concentration promote conversion of oxyhemoglobin to deoxyhemoglobin, facilitating oxygen unloading. Thus, a fall in pH causes a rightward shift of the oxygen–hemoglobin dissociation curve and decreases Hb–O₂ affinity. The Haldane effect is different: oxygenation of hemoglobin in the lungs promotes the release of CO₂ and H⁺, facilitating CO₂ excretion. Therefore, the described relationship between falling pH and decreased oxygen affinity is specifically the Bohr effect.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bohr effect → ↓ pH → ↓ Hb–O₂ affinity

  • ↓ Hb affinity → right shift of O₂ dissociation curve

  • ↑ CO₂ → promotes O₂ unloading

  • Haldane effect → oxygenation promotes CO₂ unloading

  • Right shift factors: ↑ CO₂, ↓ pH, ↑ temperature, ↑ 2,3-BPG

Exam Pearl:
Bohr effect = increased CO₂/H⁺ causes hemoglobin to release more O₂.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৭) Which of the following skin tumors is classically locally malignant with marked local tissue invasion but relatively rare metastasis?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Basal cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as rodent ulcer, is classically described as a locally malignant tumor because it is locally invasive and destructive but rarely metastasizes. It is the most common skin malignancy and commonly occurs on sun-exposed areas of the face. In contrast, squamous cell carcinoma has a definite metastatic potential, especially when arising on the lip, ear, or chronic ulcers. Malignant melanoma is highly aggressive with early lymphatic and hematogenous spread. Osteosarcoma is a high-grade malignant bone tumor with a strong tendency for hematogenous metastasis, particularly to the lungs.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Basal cell carcinoma = locally malignant

  • Rarely metastasizes

  • Commonly occurs on sun-exposed skin

  • Squamous cell carcinoma can metastasize.

  • Melanoma has the highest metastatic potential among skin cancers.

Exam Pearl:
Rodent ulcer (Basal cell carcinoma) is the classic example of a locally malignant tumor because it is locally invasive but rarely metastasizes.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৮) Blood pressure is not reliable in....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Blood pressure measurement may be unreliable in atrial fibrillation (AF) because the ventricular contractions and stroke volumes vary from beat to beat, producing variable arterial pulse pressures. This makes oscillometric and auscultatory blood pressure readings fluctuate significantly depending on which cardiac cycle is measured. Therefore, multiple measurements should be taken and averaged in patients with AF. In coarctation of the aorta, BP can differ markedly between the upper and lower limbs, but BP itself can still be measured reliably when the appropriate limb and cuff are used. Polyarteritis nodosa may cause hypertension due to renal involvement, while pulmonary stenosis does not characteristically make systemic BP measurement unreliable.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • AF → beat-to-beat variation in BP

  • Take repeated BP measurements and average them in AF.

  • Coarctation → higher upper-limb BP, lower lower-limb BP

  • AF causes an irregularly irregular pulse.

  • Automated BP devices may be less accurate with significant arrhythmia.

Exam Pearl:
Atrial fibrillation is the classic condition in which BP measurement can be unreliable because of variable stroke volume.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৯) Which is a hallmark of osteoarthritis?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Osteophyte formation is a hallmark radiographic and pathological feature of osteoarthritis (OA). OA is a degenerative joint disorder characterized by progressive loss of articular cartilage, subchondral bone changes, and formation of marginal osteophytes. Osteophytes develop as part of the reparative response at the joint margins. Restriction of movement can occur in OA, but it is a clinical consequence rather than the most characteristic structural hallmark. Syndesmophytes are classically associated with ankylosing spondylitis and other spondyloarthropathies. Generalized bodyache is nonspecific and is not a defining feature of OA.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • OA → osteophytes

  • OA → joint-space narrowing

  • OA → subchondral sclerosis and cysts

  • Ankylosing spondylitis → syndesmophytes

  • OA commonly affects weight-bearing joints, hands, and spine.

Exam Pearl:
Osteoarthritis = osteophytes + joint-space narrowing.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩০) Which amount of air remains in lung after most forceful expiration?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The amount of air remaining in the lungs after maximal/most forceful expiration is called the residual volume (RV). In a healthy adult, the standard textbook value for RV is approximately 1200 mL. This volume cannot be voluntarily expelled because the small airways close and the lungs cannot completely collapse. Residual volume is important for maintaining continuous gas exchange between breaths and preventing alveolar collapse. It is also a component of functional residual capacity (FRC), which consists of residual volume plus expiratory reserve volume. RV cannot be measured directly by simple spirometry.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Residual volume (RV) ≈ 1200 mL

  • RV = air remaining after maximal expiration

  • FRC = ERV + RV ≈ 2300 mL

  • RV cannot be measured by simple spirometry

  • RV helps prevent alveolar collapse and maintains continuous gas exchange.

Exam Pearl:
Air remaining after the most forceful expiration = residual volume ≈ 1200 mL.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩১) Diagnostic criteria of multiple myeloma excludes......?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).option2: Increased malignant plasma cells in bone marrow
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Old age is a major risk factor for multiple myeloma but is not a diagnostic criterion. Multiple myeloma is diagnosed by demonstrating a clonal plasma-cell disorder together with myeloma-defining events. Increased clonal plasma cells in the bone marrow and a monoclonal immunoglobulin (M protein) are characteristic findings. Osteolytic skeletal lesions are one of the classic CRAB manifestations of myeloma and strongly support the diagnosis. Other CRAB features include hyperCalcemia, Renal impairment, and Anemia. Modern diagnostic criteria also recognize certain biomarkers, such as ≥60% clonal bone marrow plasma cells, as myeloma-defining events.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Old age → risk factor, not diagnostic criterion

  • Bone marrow → clonal plasma cells ≥10% or plasmacytoma

  • M protein → common laboratory finding

  • Lytic bone lesions → classic CRAB feature

  • CRAB → Calcemia, Renal impairment, Anemia, Bone lesions

Exam Pearl:
Age is a risk factor for multiple myeloma, not a diagnostic criterion.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩২) CO2 has.... times more diffusion capacity than O2?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Carbon dioxide (CO₂) diffuses across the respiratory membrane approximately 20 times more readily than oxygen (O₂) when comparing their diffusion properties in the lung. This is primarily because CO₂ is much more soluble in the tissues and respiratory membrane than O₂. According to the principles of gas diffusion, diffusion capacity is influenced by gas solubility and molecular weight. Although CO₂ has a higher molecular weight than O₂, its markedly greater solubility more than compensates for this difference. However, this question has a problem: the commonly accepted physiological value is approximately 20 times, but 20 is option ঘ, not option খ. Therefore, the best scientifically accurate answer is ঘ) 20.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CO₂ diffuses ≈20× more readily than O₂

  • Main reason → much greater solubility of CO₂

  • CO₂ crosses the respiratory membrane very efficiently.

  • Diffusion depends on solubility, molecular weight, surface area, and membrane thickness.

Exam Pearl:
CO₂ is approximately 20 times more diffusible than O₂; choose 20 when available.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৩) Typical 'bamboo spine' sign in X-ray signifies....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The “bamboo spine” appearance on X-ray is a classic radiological feature of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). It results from chronic inflammation at the spinal entheses with subsequent ossification of the annulus fibrosus, producing marginal syndesmophytes that bridge adjacent vertebral bodies. Progressive syndesmophyte formation, together with vertebral fusion and ossification of spinal ligaments, produces the characteristic continuous, rigid appearance resembling a bamboo stalk. Rheumatoid arthritis primarily affects peripheral synovial joints and may cause atlantoaxial instability, but it does not typically produce bamboo spine. SLE and osteoarthritis do not characteristically cause this radiological finding.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bamboo spine → Ankylosing spondylitis

  • Due to marginal syndesmophytes

  • Associated with HLA-B27

  • Sacroiliitis is an important radiological feature.

  • AS belongs to the seronegative spondyloarthropathies.

Exam Pearl:
Bamboo spine = ankylosing spondylitis.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৪) When total vital capacity is decreased but timed vital capacity is normal?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A reduced total vital capacity (VC) with a relatively normal timed vital capacity suggests a restrictive ventilatory defect rather than an obstructive defect. Scoliosis can cause restrictive lung disease because severe spinal deformity limits expansion of the thoracic cage, reducing lung volumes, including vital capacity. However, the rate at which the available vital capacity can be expired remains relatively preserved, so timed vital capacity is normal. In contrast, bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, and emphysema are obstructive disorders in which expiratory flow is reduced, causing a reduction in timed vital capacity (e.g., FEV₁ and FEV₁/FVC).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Restrictive disease → ↓ lung volumes, relatively preserved flow ratio

  • Scoliosis → restrictive ventilatory defect

  • Obstructive diseases → asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema

  • Obstruction → ↓ FEV₁ and ↓ FEV₁/FVC

  • Restriction → ↓ TLC and VC

Exam Pearl:
Low vital capacity with preserved timed expiration points to restriction; scoliosis is the best option.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৫) Which drug is used in 1st line treatment of multiple myeloma?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thalidomide is an important anti-myeloma drug and has historically been used as part of first-line therapy for multiple myeloma, particularly in combination regimens with dexamethasone or other agents. It is an immunomodulatory drug that exerts anti-myeloma effects through several mechanisms, including inhibition of cytokine signaling and anti-angiogenic activity. Melphalan is an alkylating agent that has an important role in multiple myeloma, particularly as high-dose therapy before autologous stem-cell transplantation, but it is not generally the preferred modern frontline single agent. Prednisolone may be combined with anti-myeloma agents but is not used alone as definitive first-line therapy. Imatinib is primarily used for CML and Philadelphia chromosome-positive ALL.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thalidomide → immunomodulatory anti-myeloma drug

  • Other IMiDs → lenalidomide, pomalidomide

  • Bortezomib → proteasome inhibitor widely used in frontline regimens

  • Melphalan → alkylating agent; important in conditioning for autologous transplant

  • Imatinib → BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor → CML

Exam Pearl:
Among these options, Thalidomide is the classic first-line anti-myeloma drug.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৬) Which of the following is same in both male and female?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Tidal volume (TV) is the volume of air inspired or expired during a normal quiet breath. In standard physiological teaching, the average tidal volume is approximately 500 mL in both adult males and females. In contrast, most other lung volumes are generally somewhat lower in females because of smaller average lung size. Vital capacity, residual volume, and expiratory reserve volume therefore differ on average between males and females. The actual values vary with body size, age, and other factors, but among the given options, tidal volume is the accepted exam answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tidal volume ≈ 500 mL

  • TV is approximately same in adult male and female in standard exam physiology.

  • Male lung volumes are generally greater than female lung volumes.

  • Vital capacity = IRV + TV + ERV

  • Residual volume remains after maximal expiration.

Exam Pearl:
Among the listed lung volumes, tidal volume is classically considered similar in males and females.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৭) A 25 year old male patient presented with bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain & purpuric spot in buttocks. What may be the possible diagnosis?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Henoch–Schönlein purpura (HSP), now termed IgA vasculitis, classically presents with a tetrad of palpable purpura, abdominal pain, arthralgia/arthritis, and renal involvement. The purpura typically occurs on the lower limbs and buttocks, which is a key clue in this case. Gastrointestinal involvement can cause abdominal pain and GI bleeding, including bloody diarrhea, due to IgA-mediated small-vessel vasculitis of the intestinal tract. ITP can cause purpura and bleeding but does not characteristically cause abdominal pain with bloody diarrhea. Aplastic anemia and acute leukemia may cause bleeding due to thrombocytopenia but do not produce this characteristic clinical pattern.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HSP = IgA vasculitis

  • Classic tetrad: Purpura + abdominal pain + arthritis + renal involvement

  • Purpura → typically buttocks and lower limbs

  • GI involvement → abdominal pain and GI bleeding

  • Renal involvement → hematuria/proteinuria

Exam Pearl:
Palpable purpura on the buttocks + abdominal pain + GI bleeding = IgA vasculitis (HSP).

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৮) The only sugar normally absorbed by intestine against concentration gradient?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Glucose is absorbed by intestinal enterocytes through secondary active transport via the sodium-glucose cotransporter SGLT1 on the apical membrane. Because the Na⁺ gradient is maintained by the basolateral Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase, glucose can be transported into enterocytes against its concentration gradient. Glucose then exits the enterocyte into the blood mainly through GLUT2 by facilitated diffusion. This mechanism is clinically important because glucose-dependent Na⁺ absorption forms the basis of oral rehydration therapy. The other listed sugars do not have the same well-established physiologically important intestinal active transport mechanism against a concentration gradient.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Glucose → SGLT1 → secondary active transport

  • SGLT1 transports Na⁺ + glucose into enterocytes.

  • Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase maintains the Na⁺ gradient.

  • Glucose exits via GLUT2.

  • Oral rehydration solution works through Na⁺-glucose cotransport.

Exam Pearl:
Glucose is the classic sugar absorbed against its concentration gradient via Na⁺-dependent SGLT1.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৯) Which DMARD causes irreversible ototoxicity & retinopathy?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hydroxychloroquine is a DMARD associated with retinal toxicity, particularly maculopathy, which can become irreversible and lead to permanent visual impairment if the drug is not stopped early. The risk increases with cumulative exposure and higher doses, so regular ophthalmologic screening is recommended during long-term therapy. The question's wording includes “ototoxicity”, which is not the classic defining adverse effect of hydroxychloroquine; the key exam association is retinopathy. Methotrexate is mainly associated with hepatotoxicity and bone-marrow suppression, sulfasalazine with hypersensitivity and hematologic toxicity, and leflunomide with hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hydroxychloroquine → retinal toxicity

  • Can cause irreversible maculopathy

  • Long-term therapy requires regular ophthalmic screening

  • Methotrexate → hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression

  • Leflunomide → hepatotoxicity, teratogenicity

Exam Pearl:
Hydroxychloroquine = retinal toxicity; remember “HCQ → eye.”

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪০) Which digestive secretion contains the highest concentration of lipase?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pancreatic juice contains the major and most important digestive enzyme for triglycerides, pancreatic lipase. It is secreted by pancreatic acinar cells and acts in the small intestine, where bile salts facilitate fat emulsification and increase the surface area available for lipase action. Gastric and lingual lipases also contribute to fat digestion, but their contribution is much smaller in adults. Succus entericus contains several intestinal enzymes, but pancreatic lipase is not a characteristic component of intestinal juice. Therefore, among the listed digestive secretions, pancreatic juice contains the highest concentration and physiologically most significant lipase activity.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pancreatic lipase → major enzyme for triglyceride digestion

  • Secreted by pancreatic acinar cells

  • Acts mainly in the small intestine

  • Lingual and gastric lipases also participate in fat digestion.

  • Bile salts facilitate lipase action by emulsifying fats.

Exam Pearl:
Pancreatic juice is the major source of lipase for intestinal fat digestion.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪১) Microangiopathic hemolysis is indicated by.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA) is characterized by mechanical fragmentation of red blood cells as they pass through abnormal or narrowed small blood vessels. This produces characteristic schistocytes (red cell fragments) on the peripheral blood film. MAHA occurs in conditions such as DIC, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), and severe hypertension. Spherocytes are associated with hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune hemolytic anemia, while sickle cells indicate sickling disorders such as sickle cell disease. Hypersegmented neutrophils are characteristic of megaloblastic anemia, particularly vitamin B12 or folate deficiency.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • MAHA → schistocytes

  • Schistocytes = fragmented RBCs

  • Causes: DIC, TTP, HUS, malignant hypertension

  • Spherocytes → hereditary spherocytosis/AIHA

  • Hypersegmented neutrophils → B12/folate deficiency

Exam Pearl:
Schistocytes (red cell fragments) are the hallmark peripheral smear finding of microangiopathic hemolysis.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪২) A large greasy smelly stool usually indicates failure of digestion of which one?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A large-volume, greasy, foul-smelling stool is characteristic of steatorrhea, which indicates impaired fat digestion or absorption. Normally, dietary triglycerides are emulsified by bile salts and digested primarily by pancreatic lipase into fatty acids and monoglycerides, which are incorporated into micelles and absorbed by enterocytes. Failure of any of these processes can produce steatorrhea. Important causes include pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, bile salt deficiency, and small-intestinal mucosal disease such as coeliac disease. Carbohydrate or protein malabsorption can cause diarrhea and other symptoms but does not typically produce the characteristic greasy, bulky stool of steatorrhea.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Steatorrhea → bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stool

  • Indicates impaired fat digestion/absorption

  • Pancreatic lipase is essential for fat digestion.

  • Causes: chronic pancreatitis, biliary obstruction, coeliac disease

  • Fat malabsorption can cause deficiency of vitamins A, D, E, K

Exam Pearl:
Bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stool = steatorrhea → think fat malabsorption.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৩) Inhaled glucocorticosteroids are recommended for... COPD?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In traditional exam-oriented COPD classification, inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) are generally recommended in severe COPD, particularly in patients with recurrent exacerbations despite appropriate bronchodilator therapy. ICS are usually used in combination with long-acting bronchodilators, rather than as monotherapy. They reduce the frequency of exacerbations in selected patients, especially those with increased blood eosinophils or an asthma component. They are not routinely indicated for mild COPD. Moderate COPD is primarily managed with bronchodilators, while ICS use becomes more relevant in advanced disease with frequent exacerbations. Current COPD guidelines emphasize individualized treatment rather than severity alone.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ICS → selected COPD patients with exacerbations

  • Usually combined with LABA/LAMA, not used alone

  • Greater benefit with higher blood eosinophils

  • ICS increases the risk of pneumonia

  • Not routinely used in mild COPD.

Exam Pearl:
For this traditional MCQ, severe COPD is the best answer, but modern practice bases ICS use mainly on exacerbation history and eosinophil count rather than severity alone.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৪) Which of the following is minimally excreted in urine?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Creatine is minimally excreted in urine under normal physiological conditions. Most circulating creatine is taken up by skeletal muscle and converted to creatine phosphate, while a small amount is converted non-enzymatically to creatinine and excreted by the kidneys. In contrast, urea is the major nitrogenous waste product excreted in urine, while uric acid and creatinine are also normally present in measurable amounts. Increased urinary creatine (creatinuria) may occur in certain conditions, including pregnancy, infancy, muscle disease, and some endocrine disorders. Therefore, among the options, creatine is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Creatine → minimally excreted normally

  • Creatinine → normally excreted in urine

  • Urea → major urinary nitrogenous waste

  • Creatinine is produced from creatine phosphate in muscle

  • Creatinine is commonly used as a marker of GFR

Exam Pearl:
Creatine is minimally present in normal urine; creatinine is the normal urinary end-product of muscle creatine metabolism.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৫) Cardinal features of eczema excludes.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The cardinal features of eczema (dermatitis) include itching (pruritus), dryness, and inflammatory skin changes. Itch is a particularly prominent symptom and often leads to scratching, which can produce excoriations and further aggravate the dermatitis. Widespread dryness of the skin (xerosis) is also common, especially in atopic eczema. Although vesicles/blisters may occur in certain acute forms of eczema, such as acute vesicular eczema or pompholyx, they are not a cardinal feature of eczema as a whole. Therefore, among the given options, blisters are the best answer for the feature that is not a cardinal/general characteristic.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Eczema → itch + inflammation + dryness

  • Scratching → excoriation and lichenification

  • Atopic eczema commonly causes xerosis

  • Vesicles can occur in acute eczema, but are not universally present.

  • Chronic eczema → lichenification

Exam Pearl:
Pruritus is the hallmark symptom of eczema; blisters are not a universal feature.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৬) In renal glycosuria, the renal threshold for glucose is.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In renal glycosuria, glucose appears in the urine despite a normal blood glucose concentration because the renal tubules have a reduced capacity to reabsorb glucose. Normally, glucose is almost completely reabsorbed in the proximal tubule through SGLT2 and SGLT1 until the renal threshold is reached, typically around 180 mg/dL. In renal glycosuria, the renal threshold for glucose is lowered, so glucose begins to appear in the urine at a blood glucose concentration below the normal threshold. This may result from an inherited defect in tubular glucose transport or from conditions/drugs affecting proximal tubular glucose reabsorption.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Renal glycosuria → low renal threshold for glucose

  • Blood glucose is usually normal

  • Defect involves proximal tubular glucose reabsorption

  • Main transporter → SGLT2

  • Diabetes mellitus → glycosuria due to high plasma glucose, not a low renal threshold.

Exam Pearl:
Renal glycosuria = glycosuria at normal blood glucose because the renal glucose threshold is low.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৭) Hypertrichosis may be caused by adverse effect of which drug?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Minoxidil can cause hypertrichosis (excessive hair growth) as a well-known adverse effect. This effect occurs because minoxidil, a potassium-channel opener and potent vasodilator, can stimulate hair follicles and prolong the anagen (growth) phase of the hair cycle. Hypertrichosis is particularly common with systemic/oral minoxidil and may also occur with topical use, although topical preparations primarily cause localized hair growth. Penicillamine is associated with adverse effects such as nephrotoxicity, hematological abnormalities, and skin reactions, while vancomycin is classically associated with infusion-related “red man syndrome” and nephrotoxicity. Retinoids more commonly cause mucocutaneous dryness and other skin adverse effects.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Minoxidil → hypertrichosis

  • Minoxidil → potassium-channel opener

  • Promotes/prolongs anagen phase

  • Topical minoxidil → commonly used for androgenetic alopecia

  • Vancomycin → red man syndrome

Exam Pearl:
Minoxidil is the classic drug associated with hypertrichosis.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৮) Where acidification of urine occurs?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Urinary acidification occurs predominantly in the distal nephron, especially the distal convoluted tubule (DCT) and collecting duct, where α-intercalated cells actively secrete H⁺ into the tubular lumen. These cells contain H⁺-ATPase and H⁺/K⁺-ATPase, allowing the kidney to generate a low urinary pH and maintain systemic acid–base balance. The proximal tubule also reabsorbs most filtered bicarbonate, but it is not the principal site of final urinary acidification. The loop of Henle, particularly the thick ascending limb, contributes to acid–base handling but is not considered the main site of final urine acidification.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Final urine acidification → distal nephron

  • α-intercalated cells → H⁺ secretion

  • H⁺-ATPase is important for active H⁺ secretion.

  • PCT → major site of HCO₃⁻ reabsorption

  • Collecting duct → urine can reach a minimum pH of about 4.5

Exam Pearl:
DCT and collecting duct are the key sites of final urinary acidification.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৯) A 20 years old female presented with loss of interest in activity, decreased appetite, early morning awakening. What is most probable diagnosis?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The patient has several classic features of a major depressive episode, including loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia), decreased appetite, and early-morning awakening (terminal insomnia). Early-morning awakening is particularly associated with melancholic depression. A diagnosis of major depressive disorder requires a persistent depressed mood and/or loss of interest or pleasure, accompanied by additional symptoms such as sleep or appetite disturbance, low energy, impaired concentration, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, or suicidal thoughts, typically lasting at least 2 weeks and causing significant functional impairment. Conversion disorder produces neurological symptoms inconsistent with recognized disease, while anxiety and stress disorders have different predominant symptom patterns.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Depression → anhedonia + sleep/appetite disturbance

  • Early-morning awakening → classic melancholic feature

  • Major depressive episode → symptoms typically ≥2 weeks

  • Depression may cause decreased appetite and weight loss

  • Always assess for suicidal ideation clinically.

Exam Pearl:
Anhedonia + early-morning awakening + appetite loss strongly suggests depression.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫০) In diabetic ketosis there is decreased metabolic breakdown of....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), insulin deficiency causes a marked reduction in glucose utilization and metabolism by peripheral tissues, despite elevated blood glucose levels. At the same time, insulin deficiency increases lipolysis, leading to increased release of free fatty acids, which are transported to the liver and converted into ketone bodies. Therefore, fatty-acid breakdown is increased, not decreased. Protein catabolism and gluconeogenesis are also increased, further contributing to hyperglycemia. Glycerol released from triglyceride breakdown is also used as a substrate for gluconeogenesis. Thus, among the options, decreased metabolic breakdown/utilization of glucose is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • DKA → ↓ insulin

  • ↓ glucose utilization → hyperglycemia

  • ↑ lipolysis → ↑ free fatty acids

  • ↑ fatty-acid oxidation → ketone bodies

  • Ketone bodies → acetoacetate, β-hydroxybutyrate, acetone

  • Protein catabolism → increased gluconeogenesis

Exam Pearl:
DKA = decreased glucose utilization + increased fat breakdown and ketogenesis.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫১) 'Pansystolic murmur in mitral area which radiates to left axilla' - occurs in..........?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A pansystolic (holosystolic) murmur heard best at the apex/mitral area and radiating to the left axilla is the classic auscultatory finding of mitral regurgitation (MR). It results from backward flow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium throughout ventricular systole because the mitral valve fails to close properly. The murmur is typically high-pitched and blowing and begins with S1 and continues through S2. In contrast, mitral stenosis produces a mid-diastolic rumbling murmur, aortic stenosis produces a crescendo-decrescendo ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids, and aortic regurgitation produces an early diastolic decrescendo murmur.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • MR → pansystolic murmur at apex → left axilla

  • MR murmur → blowing, high-pitched

  • MS → mid-diastolic rumbling + opening snap

  • AS → ejection systolic → carotids

  • AR → early diastolic decrescendo

Exam Pearl:
Pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla = Mitral regurgitation.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫২) Betz cells are predominantly present in....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Betz cells are large pyramidal neurons located predominantly in layer V of the primary motor cortex, which is situated in the precentral gyrus of the frontal lobe. Their axons contribute to the corticospinal tract, particularly the fibers involved in voluntary motor control of the limbs and trunk. Betz cells are among the largest neurons in the human cerebral cortex. The postcentral gyrus contains the primary somatosensory cortex, while the hippocampus and amygdala are primarily involved in memory and emotion, respectively, and do not contain the characteristic concentration of Betz cells.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Betz cells → precentral gyrus

  • Located mainly in layer V of motor cortex

  • Large pyramidal cells

  • Axons contribute to the corticospinal tract

  • Precentral gyrus → primary motor cortex

  • Postcentral gyrus → primary somatosensory cortex

Exam Pearl:
Betz cells = giant pyramidal cells of the primary motor cortex in the precentral gyrus.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৩) When there is no response to antihypertensive drugs, it is called..........?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Resistant hypertension refers to blood pressure that remains above the target despite treatment with an appropriate regimen of three antihypertensive drugs of different classes, ideally including a diuretic, at maximally tolerated doses. It may also refer to blood pressure that is controlled only with four or more medications. Before diagnosing resistant hypertension, adherence, accurate BP measurement, white-coat hypertension, and secondary causes should be considered. Refractory hypertension is a rarer and more severe condition in which BP remains uncontrolled despite treatment with five or more antihypertensive medications, including a long-acting thiazide-type diuretic and a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Resistant hypertension → uncontrolled despite ≥3 drugs

  • Regimen should usually include a diuretic

  • Controlled BP requiring ≥4 drugs also qualifies.

  • Refractory hypertension → uncontrolled despite ≥5 drugs

  • Always exclude poor adherence and secondary hypertension.

Exam Pearl:
Uncontrolled BP despite 3 appropriate antihypertensive drugs = resistant hypertension.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৪) At the time of ovulation Graafian follicles contain....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
At the time of ovulation, the Graafian follicle contains a secondary oocyte, not an ovum or primary oocyte. The primary oocyte completes meiosis I shortly before ovulation, producing a secondary oocyte and the first polar body. The secondary oocyte then begins meiosis II but becomes arrested at metaphase II. It is this secondary oocyte that is released during ovulation. Meiosis II is completed only if fertilization occurs, after which the mature ovum is formed. Oogonia are present during fetal life and do not normally persist after birth.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ovulation → secondary oocyte

  • Secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II

  • Primary oocyte → completes meiosis I just before ovulation

  • Meiosis II completes only after fertilization

  • Oogonia → present during fetal life

Exam Pearl:
Ovulated cell = secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase II.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৫) Which antihypertensive is contraindicated in gout?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thiazide diuretics are generally avoided or used cautiously in patients with gout because they decrease renal urate excretion, causing hyperuricemia and potentially precipitating gout attacks. They increase proximal tubular reabsorption of uric acid, partly because volume contraction enhances urate reabsorption. Loop diuretics can also increase serum uric acid and may worsen gout, but thiazides are the classic exam answer. Among the alternatives, losartan, an ARB, is actually beneficial in hyperuricemia because it has a uricosuric effect. ACE inhibitors do not have the characteristic urate-raising effect associated with thiazide diuretics.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thiazides → ↑ uric acid → gout

  • Loop diuretics can also cause hyperuricemia.

  • Losartan → uricosuric effect

  • Thiazides decrease renal uric acid excretion.

  • Avoid unnecessary thiazide use in patients with recurrent gout.

Exam Pearl:
Gout + antihypertensive → avoid thiazides; remember losartan is uricosuric.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৬) What type of collagen fibres are present in cartilage?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Type II collagen is the principal collagen found in cartilage, particularly hyaline and elastic cartilage. It forms a network of fibrils that provides tensile strength and supports the cartilage matrix against mechanical stress. In hyaline cartilage, type II collagen is embedded within a matrix rich in proteoglycans and water, allowing cartilage to resist compression. Type I collagen is predominant in bone, tendons, ligaments, and fibrocartilage (although fibrocartilage also contains substantial type II collagen). Type III collagen forms reticular fibers, while type IV collagen is a major component of basement membranes rather than cartilage.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cartilage → Type II collagen

  • Bone → Type I

  • Tendon → Type I

  • Reticular fibers → Type III

  • Basement membrane → Type IV

  • Fibrocartilage → predominantly Type I, with type II also present

Exam Pearl:
Type II collagen = cartilage.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৭) Which component of vitamin B complex doesn't show neurological manifestation?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the listed B-complex vitamins, niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency classically causes pellagra, characterized by the 3 Ds: dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia. Although severe niacin deficiency can produce neuropsychiatric manifestations such as confusion and dementia, it is not classically associated with a primary neurological syndrome in the way several other B-vitamin deficiencies are. Thiamine (B1) deficiency causes beriberi and Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome, while pyridoxine (B6) deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy. Riboflavin (B2) deficiency mainly causes mucocutaneous manifestations such as cheilosis, angular stomatitis, glossitis, and dermatitis. Therefore, if the question asks for the B vitamin classically considered not to cause a neurological manifestation, riboflavin is actually the more appropriate answer.

Ambiguity: The question is poorly worded because severe niacin deficiency can cause dementia. If “neurological manifestation” means a classic primary neurological deficiency syndrome, the best answer is খ) Riboflavin.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • B1 → Wernicke–Korsakoff, neuropathy

  • B2 → cheilosis, angular stomatitis, glossitis

  • B3 → pellagra: dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia

  • B6 → peripheral neuropathy, seizures

  • B12 → neurological dysfunction + megaloblastic anemia

Exam Pearl:
Among these options, Riboflavin (B2) is the best answer for “no characteristic neurological manifestation.”

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৮) Which is the area of maximum visual acuity in retina?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The fovea centralis is the area of maximum visual acuity in the retina. It is a small depression located within the macula lutea and contains an exceptionally high density of cones, with virtually no rods. The fovea has minimal overlying retinal layers and an absence of retinal blood vessels in the central foveal avascular zone, allowing light to reach the photoreceptors with minimal scattering. The macula lutea is responsible for central vision but the foveal center provides the highest visual resolution. The optic disc is the physiological blind spot because it lacks photoreceptors, while the ora serrata marks the anterior limit of the photosensitive retina.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Maximum visual acuity → fovea centralis

  • Fovea lies within the macula lutea

  • Fovea → predominantly cones

  • Optic disc → blind spot

  • Ora serrata → anterior boundary of neural retina

Exam Pearl:
Fovea centralis = maximum visual acuity.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৯) Tender, red or purplish skin lesions that occur in the cold and wet environment is termed as........?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Chilblains (pernio) are inflammatory skin lesions caused by prolonged exposure to cold and damp conditions. They typically present as tender, itchy, red or purplish lesions, usually affecting the fingers, toes, ears, or other acral areas. They result from an abnormal vascular response to cold, with inflammation and impaired microcirculation. Trench foot/immersion foot occurs after prolonged exposure of the feet to cold, wet conditions and typically causes swelling, numbness, pain, and tissue injury. Frostbite results from actual freezing of tissues and is more severe. Thus, the description of tender red or purplish lesions in a cold, wet environment is characteristic of chilblains.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Chilblains = pernio

  • Cold + damp exposure → red/purplish tender lesions

  • Common sites → fingers and toes

  • Trench foot → prolonged cold, wet feet

  • Frostbite → freezing of tissue

Exam Pearl:
Cold + wet + tender red/purple skin lesions = chilblains (pernio).

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬০) Which is primary lymphoid organ?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The thymus is a primary lymphoid organ, where immature T lymphocytes undergo maturation and selection. The other major primary lymphoid organ is the bone marrow, where hematopoiesis occurs and B lymphocytes mature. In contrast, the spleen and lymph nodes are secondary lymphoid organs, where mature lymphocytes encounter antigens and initiate immune responses. The liver is not classified as a primary lymphoid organ, although it has important hematological and immune functions. Therefore, among the given options, the thymus is the only primary lymphoid organ.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Primary lymphoid organs → bone marrow + thymus

  • Thymus → T-cell maturation

  • Bone marrow → B-cell maturation

  • Spleen → secondary lymphoid organ; filters blood

  • Lymph node → secondary lymphoid organ; filters lymph

Exam Pearl:
Primary lymphoid organs = thymus and bone marrow.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬১) Which is ECG finding in hypothermia?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A J wave (Osborn wave) is the classic ECG finding associated with hypothermia. It appears as a positive deflection at the junction between the QRS complex and ST segment, producing a characteristic notch or hump at the J point. J waves become more prominent as core temperature falls, although their presence and magnitude do not correlate perfectly with temperature. Other ECG changes in hypothermia include sinus bradycardia, prolonged PR/QT intervals, and atrial or ventricular arrhythmias. A U wave is more characteristically associated with hypokalemia, whereas E wave and L wave are not recognized classic ECG findings of hypothermia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypothermia → J (Osborn) wave

  • J wave occurs at the J point

  • Other findings → bradycardia, prolonged QT, arrhythmias

  • Hypokalemia → prominent U waves

  • Severe hypothermia → increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias

Exam Pearl:
Hypothermia + ECG = J wave (Osborn wave).

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬২) Which papillae of tongue contain no taste bud?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Filiform papillae are the most numerous papillae on the tongue and are primarily responsible for mechanical functions, helping grip and manipulate food. They do not contain taste buds, making them the correct answer. In contrast, fungiform papillae contain taste buds mainly on their dorsal surface, circumvallate papillae contain numerous taste buds along their lateral walls, and foliate papillae contain taste buds within their epithelial folds. Filiform papillae are also distinctive because they are covered by a keratinized epithelium, giving the tongue its rough texture.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Filiform → no taste buds

  • Fungiform → taste buds on dorsal surface

  • Circumvallate → numerous taste buds on lateral walls

  • Foliate → taste buds in epithelial folds

  • Filiform → mechanical function

Exam Pearl:
Filiform papillae = no taste buds.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৩) Stage of resolution in CAP is characterized by…..?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), the resolution phase occurs as the inflammatory exudate within the alveoli is cleared and normal aeration is restored. Crepitations (crackles), which occur due to reopening of fluid-filled or collapsed small airways and alveoli, gradually disappear during resolution. Rhonchi are mainly caused by secretions or airway narrowing in larger airways and are not a defining feature of pneumonia resolution. During the active consolidation phase, bronchial breathing, increased vocal resonance, and crepitations may be present. As the consolidation resolves, these abnormal breath sounds progressively disappear, although radiological resolution may lag behind clinical recovery.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pneumonia → crepitations/crackles commonly present

  • Resolution → disappearance of crepitations

  • Consolidation → bronchial breathing + increased vocal resonance

  • Radiological resolution may occur later than clinical improvement

  • Rhonchi → usually related to airway secretions/obstruction

Exam Pearl:
Resolution of pneumonia → disappearance of crepitations.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৪) Umbilical cord contain all except...?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The umbilical cord develops from the connecting stalk and contains structures derived from the extraembryonic tissues. It normally contains the umbilical vessels, allantoic duct/remnant, vitellointestinal (vitelline) duct remnant, and extraembryonic mesoderm, which forms Wharton’s jelly. The yolk sac itself is not a component of the umbilical cord. The yolk sac is an extraembryonic membrane that is connected to the developing midgut through the vitelline duct. During development, the vitelline duct normally disappears; persistence may result in a Meckel diverticulum.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Umbilical cord → 2 umbilical arteries + 1 umbilical vein

  • Contains Wharton’s jelly

  • Allantoic remnant → present

  • Vitellointestinal duct → embryological connection with yolk sac

  • Yolk sac itself → not contained in the umbilical cord

Exam Pearl:
Umbilical cord contains the vitelline duct remnant, not the yolk sac itself.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৫) What is the indications for emergency surgery in peptic ulcer disease??
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).option4: Persistent ulceration despite adequate medical therapy
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Perforation of a peptic ulcer is a classic indication for emergency surgery because it causes leakage of gastric or duodenal contents into the peritoneal cavity, leading to peritonitis, sepsis, and potentially life-threatening shock. It requires urgent resuscitation, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and usually operative closure with an omental patch or other appropriate surgical management. Gastric outlet obstruction, recurrent ulcer after gastric surgery, and persistent ulceration despite adequate medical therapy may require elective or planned surgical intervention in selected cases, but they are not typically indications for emergency surgery. Therefore, perforation is the single best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Perforated peptic ulcer → emergency surgical indication

  • Perforation → chemical then bacterial peritonitis

  • Initial management → resuscitation + antibiotics + urgent surgical assessment

  • Gastric outlet obstruction → usually elective management

  • Persistent/recurrent ulcer → investigate for H. pylori, NSAIDs, and other causes

Exam Pearl:
Peptic ulcer + perforation = surgical emergency.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৬) Prechordal plate is a thickening in.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The prechordal plate is a localized thickening of endoderm at the cranial end of the embryonic disc. It develops in the midline, just rostral to the notochordal process, and plays an important role in establishing the cranial axis and head development. It also contributes to signaling that influences the development of the forebrain and surrounding structures. The prechordal plate should be distinguished from the notochord, which develops from mesoderm. The ectoderm forms the neural plate and subsequently the neural tube under inductive influences from the axial mesoderm and prechordal region.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Prechordal plate → endodermal thickening

  • Located cranial to the notochord

  • Important in head and forebrain development

  • Notochord → derived from axial mesoderm

  • Neural plate → derived from ectoderm

Exam Pearl:
Prechordal plate = localized endodermal thickening at the cranial end.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৭) What is the cause of Pel-Ebstein fever?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pel-Ebstein fever is the classic, periodically recurring fever pattern historically associated with Hodgkin lymphoma. It is characterized by episodes of fever lasting several days followed by periods of normal temperature, with the cycle potentially recurring over weeks. Although the association is classically taught in examinations, this fever pattern is not considered specific or diagnostic of Hodgkin lymphoma in modern clinical practice. Hodgkin lymphoma may also present with painless lymphadenopathy, weight loss, night sweats, and pruritus.
