Tuberculosis and malaria can cause recurrent or periodic fever patterns, but Pel-Ebstein fever is classically linked to Hodgkin disease.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pel-Ebstein fever → Hodgkin lymphoma

  • Hodgkin lymphoma → painless lymphadenopathy

  • B symptoms → fever, night sweats, weight loss

  • Pel-Ebstein pattern is not specific or diagnostic

  • Malaria → characteristic periodic fever according to species

Exam Pearl:
Pel-Ebstein fever is classically associated with Hodgkin lymphoma.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৮) Posterior epithelium of cornea develops from.......?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The posterior epithelium (endothelium) of the cornea, also called the corneal endothelium, develops from neural crest cells, which are derived from ectomesenchyme of neural crest origin and are therefore generally classified under mesoderm-like mesenchymal derivatives in traditional embryology exam schemes. The anterior epithelium of the cornea develops from surface ectoderm, whereas the corneal stroma and endothelium arise largely from neural crest-derived mesenchyme. Among the options given, mesoderm is the accepted examination answer. Neuroectoderm forms structures such as the retina and optic nerve rather than the corneal endothelium.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Corneal epithelium → surface ectoderm

  • Corneal stroma → neural crest-derived mesenchyme

  • Corneal endothelium → neural crest-derived cells

  • Retina → neuroectoderm

  • Neural crest cells → important source of anterior-segment mesenchyme

Exam Pearl:
Corneal endothelium = neural crest-derived mesenchyme; in this MCQ, choose mesoderm.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৯) Non-gastrointestinal causes of vomiting excludes..... ?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Diverticulitis is a gastrointestinal condition involving inflammation of a colonic diverticulum and can cause abdominal pain, fever, altered bowel habits, and sometimes nausea or vomiting. Therefore, it is the best answer for the condition that is not a non-gastrointestinal cause of vomiting. In contrast, acute renal failure may cause vomiting due to uremia, while Addison’s disease can cause nausea and vomiting due to adrenal insufficiency and associated metabolic disturbances. Hyperemesis gravidarum is a pregnancy-related systemic condition characterized by severe, persistent vomiting. Thus, among the options, diverticulitis is the gastrointestinal cause.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Uremia → nausea and vomiting

  • Addison’s disease → GI symptoms + hypotension + hyperpigmentation

  • Hyperemesis gravidarum → severe vomiting in pregnancy

  • Diverticulitis → gastrointestinal cause

  • Always consider metabolic, endocrine, renal, CNS, and drug-related causes of vomiting.

Exam Pearl:
Diverticulitis is the GI cause; the other options are classified as non-GI/systemic causes of vomiting.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭০) Which flexure appears first in development of brain?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The mesencephalic (cephalic) flexure is the first major flexure to appear during embryonic development of the brain. It develops at the junction between the mesencephalon (midbrain) and the forebrain, producing a ventral bend of the developing neural tube. Subsequently, the cervical flexure develops between the hindbrain and spinal cord, followed later by the pontine flexure within the hindbrain. These flexures are important in establishing the characteristic shape and orientation of the developing brain.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • First flexure → mesencephalic (cephalic)

  • Mesencephalic flexure → at the midbrain

  • Cervical flexure → between hindbrain and spinal cord

  • Pontine flexure → develops later in the hindbrain

  • Flexures help establish the final configuration of the brain.

Exam Pearl:
Mesencephalic (cephalic) flexure appears first.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭১) What is clinical finding in a patient with right sided pleural effusion?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).option1: Restricted chest movement in left side
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).option2: Vocal fremitus reduced in left side
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).option4: Breath sound diminished in left side
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In a large right-sided pleural effusion, accumulated fluid occupies the right pleural cavity and exerts a mass effect, pushing the mediastinum and trachea toward the opposite (left) side. On examination, there is reduced chest expansion, decreased vocal fremitus, and diminished breath sounds over the right side—not the left. The trachea usually remains central with a small effusion but may shift away from the affected side when the effusion is large. In contrast, conditions causing significant volume loss, such as lung collapse, tend to pull the trachea toward the affected side.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Large right pleural effusion → trachea shifts left

  • Pleural effusion → ↓ vocal fremitus

  • Pleural effusion → ↓ breath sounds

  • Pleural effusion → ↓ chest expansion on affected side

  • Large effusion → tracheal shift away from the lesion

Exam Pearl:
Large pleural effusion pushes the trachea away from the affected side.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭২) Sinus venosus contributes to the development of....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The sinus venosus contributes primarily to the smooth posterior part of the right atrium, called the sinus venarum. During cardiac development, the right horn of the sinus venosus becomes incorporated into the right atrium as venous return shifts toward the right side. The left horn largely forms the coronary sinus and oblique vein of the left atrium. The trabeculated anterior part of the right atrium develops from the primitive atrium, while the smooth posterior part is derived from the sinus venosus. The pulmonary trunk develops from the truncus arteriosus, and the pulmonary veins develop separately from the common pulmonary vein.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sinus venosus → smooth part of right atrium

  • Right horn → sinus venarum

  • Left horn → coronary sinus

  • Primitive atrium → trabeculated parts of atria

  • Truncus arteriosus → pulmonary trunk + ascending aorta

Exam Pearl:
Sinus venosus → smooth posterior wall of the right atrium.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৩) Antibiotic coverage in lung abscess should be given...?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A lung abscess generally requires a prolonged course of antibiotics because the infection involves a localized cavity containing necrotic material, where antibiotic penetration may be relatively poor. Treatment is usually continued for approximately 4–6 weeks, with duration guided by clinical and radiological response. Initial therapy should provide good coverage against anaerobic organisms and other likely pathogens, commonly using a β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor such as ampicillin-sulbactam. Clinical improvement usually precedes complete radiological resolution, so antibiotics are continued until the patient is clinically well and imaging shows substantial resolution. Short courses of 2–3 weeks are generally inadequate, whereas 6 months is excessive for an uncomplicated responding abscess.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Lung abscess → prolonged antibiotic therapy

  • Typical duration → 4–6 weeks

  • Important organisms → anaerobes

  • Common treatment → β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor

  • Duration should be guided by clinical and radiological response

Exam Pearl:
Lung abscess usually needs about 4–6 weeks of antibiotic therapy.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৪) Which part of pancreas develops from ventral pancreatic bud?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The ventral pancreatic bud rotates posteriorly around the duodenum and fuses with the dorsal pancreatic bud. It forms the uncinate process and the inferior part of the pancreatic head. The dorsal pancreatic bud forms the remaining, larger portion of the pancreas, including most of the head, body, and tail. Therefore, among the given options, the uncinate process is the best answer. The pancreatic duct system also reflects this embryological origin: the ventral duct contributes to the main pancreatic duct after fusion with the dorsal ductal system.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ventral pancreatic bud → uncinate process + inferior head

  • Dorsal pancreatic bud → most of head, body, and tail

  • Ventral bud rotates posteriorly

  • Pancreatic buds fuse around the 7th week

  • Main pancreatic duct → formed by fusion of ventral and dorsal duct systems

Exam Pearl:
Ventral pancreatic bud = uncinate process (and inferior part of head).

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৫) KF rings are found in....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Kayser–Fleischer (KF) rings are deposits of copper in Descemet’s membrane at the peripheral cornea and are classically associated with Wilson’s disease. Wilson’s disease results from impaired biliary copper excretion due to ATP7B dysfunction, leading to copper accumulation, particularly in the liver, brain, and cornea. KF rings are especially common in patients with neurological or hepatic manifestations, although their absence does not exclude Wilson’s disease. Hemochromatosis involves excess iron, while Gilbert’s syndrome causes mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Budd–Chiari syndrome results from hepatic venous outflow obstruction and is unrelated to corneal copper deposition.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • KF rings → Wilson’s disease

  • Caused by copper deposition

  • Site → Descemet’s membrane

  • Wilson’s disease → ATP7B mutation

  • Neurological Wilson’s disease → KF rings are highly prevalent

  • Hemochromatosis → iron overload

Exam Pearl:
Kayser–Fleischer ring = corneal copper deposition = Wilson’s disease.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৬) The median umbilical ligament is a remnant of......?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The median umbilical ligament is the fibrous remnant of the urachus, which connects the fetal bladder to the umbilicus. Embryologically, the urachus develops from the allantois and the superior part of the fetal bladder. After birth, the urachus normally obliterates and becomes the median umbilical ligament, located in the midline between the bladder and umbilicus. It should be distinguished from the medial umbilical ligaments, which are remnants of the umbilical arteries. Paroophoron and epoophoron are remnants of the mesonephric system in females and are unrelated to the median umbilical ligament.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Urachus → median umbilical ligament

  • Urachus → embryological remnant of allantois

  • Median umbilical ligament → bladder apex to umbilicus

  • Umbilical arteries → medial umbilical ligaments

  • Patent urachus → urine discharge from umbilicus

Exam Pearl:
Median umbilical ligament = obliterated urachus.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৭) Which is not a systemic complications of acute pancreatitis?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pleural effusion, SIRS, and hypoxia are recognized systemic complications of acute pancreatitis. Pancreatic inflammation can trigger a systemic inflammatory response, causing increased vascular permeability, pulmonary capillary leak, and respiratory complications such as hypoxemia and pleural effusion. Hyperglycemia, however, is primarily a metabolic/endocrine consequence of pancreatic injury, particularly impaired insulin secretion from islet-cell damage and the stress response. Therefore, in the context of a question asking specifically for a systemic complication, hyperglycemia is the best answer. It is important to note that severe acute pancreatitis can produce both systemic inflammatory and metabolic complications.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute pancreatitis → SIRS

  • Pulmonary complications → hypoxia, ARDS, pleural effusion

  • Pancreatic endocrine injury → hyperglycemia

  • Severe SIRS → risk of multiorgan failure

  • Hypocalcemia can occur due to fat saponification

Exam Pearl:
Pleural effusion, SIRS, and hypoxia are systemic complications; hyperglycemia is primarily a metabolic complication.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৮) What type of joint 1st sternocostal joint is?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The 1st sternocostal joint is a primary cartilaginous joint (synchondrosis) formed between the first costal cartilage and the manubrium of the sternum. It is essentially immovable and is connected by hyaline cartilage. In contrast, the 2nd–7th sternocostal joints are synovial plane joints (with the 2nd having a more complex relationship with the manubrium-sternal junction). A symphysis is a secondary cartilaginous joint containing fibrocartilage, such as the pubic symphysis. Syndesmosis is a fibrous joint connected by ligaments or an interosseous membrane, while gomphosis is the joint between a tooth and its socket.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • 1st sternocostal joint → synchondrosis

  • 1st costal cartilage → manubrium

  • 1st sternocostal joint → primary cartilaginous

  • 2nd–7th sternocostal joints → mainly synovial

  • Pubic symphysis → symphysis

Exam Pearl:
1st sternocostal joint = synchondrosis.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৯) What is the lining epithelium of tonsil?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The palatine tonsil is covered by nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which is continuous with the lining of the oropharynx. Its deep surface contains numerous crypts that increase the surface area for interaction between antigens and lymphoid tissue. The epithelium is supported by lymphoid tissue containing lymphoid follicles and germinal centers. Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium is typical of areas such as the skin and parts of the oral mucosa exposed to significant mechanical stress. Simple squamous and simple columnar epithelia are not the characteristic lining of the palatine tonsil.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Palatine tonsil → nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium

  • Palatine tonsil → numerous crypts

  • Contains lymphoid follicles with germinal centers

  • Nasopharyngeal (pharyngeal) tonsil → pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium

  • Lingual tonsil → mainly stratified squamous epithelium

Exam Pearl:
Palatine tonsil = nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮০) What is the cause of sodium & water depletion due to renal loss?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Diuretic therapy causes renal loss of sodium and water by increasing urinary excretion of Na⁺ and water. Loop and thiazide diuretics inhibit sodium reabsorption at different sites of the nephron, leading to increased natriuresis and diuresis. In contrast, vomiting causes extrarenal loss of fluid and electrolytes through the gastrointestinal tract. Pancreatitis can cause substantial fluid sequestration into the retroperitoneum and peritoneal cavity (“third spacing”), while burns cause fluid and electrolyte loss primarily through damaged skin and increased capillary permeability. Therefore, diuretic therapy is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Diuretics → renal Na⁺ and water loss

  • Vomiting → GI loss

  • Burns → cutaneous loss + capillary leak

  • Pancreatitis → third-space fluid loss

  • Loop diuretics → marked natriuresis

Exam Pearl:
Renal sodium + water depletion = think diuretic therapy.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮১) Branches of right coronary artery excludes....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The right coronary artery (RCA) commonly gives rise to the SA nodal artery, right marginal artery, and AV nodal artery. The circumflex artery, however, is a major branch of the left coronary artery (LCA), not the RCA. The RCA typically originates from the right aortic sinus and courses in the right atrioventricular groove. It supplies much of the right atrium and ventricle and, in most people, contributes to the blood supply of the AV node. The exact origin of the SA nodal artery is variable, but it most commonly arises from the RCA.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • RCA → SA nodal artery

  • RCA → AV nodal artery

  • RCA → right marginal artery

  • LCA → LAD + circumflex

  • Circumflex → mainly left atrium and lateral/posterior LV

Exam Pearl:
Circumflex is a branch of the left coronary artery, not the RCA.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮২) Which process makes the bacteria tasty to the leukocyte?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Opsonization is the process by which bacteria are coated with opsonins, making them easier for leukocytes, particularly neutrophils and macrophages, to recognize, bind, and phagocytose. Important opsonins include IgG, C3b, and collectins such as mannose-binding lectin. Leukocytes possess receptors for these molecules, allowing more efficient attachment and ingestion of the microorganism. Margination refers to leukocytes moving toward the endothelial surface, diapedesis is their passage through the vessel wall, and chemotaxis is directed migration toward a chemical stimulus. Thus, the process that makes bacteria “tasty” or easier to eat is opsonization.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Opsonization → enhanced phagocytosis

  • Major opsonins → IgG and C3b

  • C3b receptor on phagocytes → CR1

  • Margination → leukocyte moves to vessel periphery

  • Diapedesis → leukocyte crosses endothelium

  • Chemotaxis → directed movement toward inflammatory signals

Exam Pearl:
Opsonization makes bacteria “tasty” to phagocytes.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৩) Which lymph nodes primarily drain the testes?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The testes primarily drain lymphatically to the para-aortic (lumbar) lymph nodes because the testes develop embryologically on the posterior abdominal wall and descend into the scrotum while retaining their original lymphatic drainage. The lymphatics accompany the testicular vessels through the spermatic cord toward the lumbar nodes. This differs from the scrotum, which drains mainly to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes. External and internal iliac nodes are not the primary lymphatic drainage sites of the testes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Testes → para-aortic (lumbar) nodes

  • Scrotum → superficial inguinal nodes

  • Testicular lymphatics follow the testicular vessels

  • Testicular descent does not change its primary lymphatic drainage

Exam Pearl:
Testis = para-aortic nodes; scrotum = superficial inguinal nodes.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৪) Earliest transient change following tissue injury will be......?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The earliest transient leukocyte change following acute tissue injury or inflammation is typically neutrophilia. In the early phase of the inflammatory response, catecholamines and glucocorticoids promote the release of neutrophils from the marginal pool into the circulating blood, producing a rapid rise in the neutrophil count. This is followed by recruitment of neutrophils from the bloodstream into the injured tissue. Later, depending on the cause and duration of inflammation, other leukocytes such as monocytes may become more prominent. Neutropenia, monocytosis, and lymphocytosis are not the characteristic earliest transient response to acute tissue injury.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute tissue injury → early neutrophilia

  • Early neutrophilia partly results from demargination

  • Neutrophils are the predominant early leukocytes in acute inflammation

  • Monocytes become more important later

  • Severe infection may eventually cause neutropenia due to exhaustion/overwhelming demand

Exam Pearl:
Acute tissue injury → early transient neutrophilia.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৫) Abdominal aorta bifurcates at....level?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The abdominal aorta bifurcates into the right and left common iliac arteries at the level of L4 vertebra, usually slightly below the level of the umbilicus. This is an important anatomical landmark used in abdominal and vascular examinations. The aorta enters the abdomen through the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm at approximately T12 and descends anterior to the vertebral bodies. It terminates by dividing into the common iliac arteries at L4. The inferior mesenteric artery arises around L3, while the aortic bifurcation is classically remembered as L4.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Aortic hiatus → T12

  • Celiac trunk → T12

  • Superior mesenteric artery → L1

  • Renal arteries → L1–L2

  • Inferior mesenteric artery → L3

  • Aortic bifurcation → L4

Exam Pearl:
Abdominal aorta bifurcates at L4.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৬) Which is essential for tumor metastasis?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Angiogenesis is essential for the growth and metastasis of most solid tumors because an expanding tumor requires a blood supply to obtain oxygen and nutrients and to gain access to the circulation. Tumor cells can stimulate angiogenesis by releasing pro-angiogenic factors, particularly vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Newly formed, abnormal tumor-associated vessels also facilitate tumor cells entering the bloodstream (intravasation), supporting hematogenous metastasis. Tumorigenesis refers broadly to the development of a tumor rather than specifically enabling metastasis. Apoptosis generally suppresses tumor progression, while inhibition of tyrosine kinase activity is a therapeutic strategy for certain cancers rather than a requirement for metastasis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Angiogenesis → essential for solid tumor growth and metastasis

  • Major mediator → VEGF

  • Angiogenesis provides nutrients and vascular access

  • Tumor invasion → basement membrane/ECM degradation

  • Metastasis → invasion → intravasation → circulation → extravasation → colonization

Exam Pearl:
No adequate angiogenesis → limited tumor growth and metastatic potential.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৭) Which structure is NOT contained within the broad ligament of the uterus?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The broad ligament is a double-layered fold of peritoneum that supports the uterus and contains several important structures. It encloses the uterine tube, uterine vessels, lymphatics, and parts of the ovarian ligament and round ligament. The ovary is not contained within the broad ligament; instead, it is attached to the posterior surface of the broad ligament by the mesovarium. The ureter is also closely related to the broad ligament but is not considered a true content. The ovarian vessels pass through the suspensory ligament of the ovary rather than being a content of the broad ligament.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

Broad ligament → peritoneal fold supporting uterus
Contains → uterine tube, vessels, lymphatics
Ovary → attached by mesovarium
Ureter passes close to uterine artery → “water under the bridge”
Suspensory ligament → contains ovarian vessels
Exam Pearl:
Ovary is attached to the broad ligament but is not a true content of it.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৮) Echinocytes are type of....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Echinocytes are abnormal forms of red blood cells (RBCs) characterized by numerous small, regularly spaced projections on their surface, giving them a “burr cell” appearance. They may be seen as an artifact due to improper sample handling or drying of the blood film. True echinocytosis can also occur in conditions such as uremia, pyruvate kinase deficiency, and electrolyte disturbances. Echinocytes should be distinguished from acanthocytes, which have fewer, irregularly distributed projections. Lymphocytes, monocytes, and platelets do not develop the characteristic echinocyte morphology.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Echinocyte = burr cell = RBC

  • Echinocytes → regular, evenly spaced projections

  • Acanthocytes → irregular projections

  • Echinocytosis → may occur in uremia

  • Blood film artifact is a common cause

Exam Pearl:
Echinocyte (burr cell) = abnormal RBC with regular projections.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৯) Prostatic urethra emerges from which surface of prostate?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The prostatic urethra passes through the prostate from its base to apex and is positioned centrally within the gland. Anatomically, the urethra enters the prostate at the base and emerges from the apex, which is directed inferiorly. The prostate has anterior, posterior, and inferolateral surfaces; however, in standard anatomical descriptions, the urethra is located close to the anterior aspect of the gland rather than emerging from the posterior surface. Therefore, this MCQ is poorly worded, because the urethra does not truly “emerge from” a named surface in the simple sense implied by the options. If forced to select from these options, posterior is not anatomically ideal.

Ambiguity: The question is flawed because the prostatic urethra traverses the prostate rather than simply emerging from one surface.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯০) All of the following are chromosomal breakage syndrome except.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome (EDS) is a group of inherited connective-tissue disorders primarily caused by abnormalities of collagen synthesis or structure. It is not classified as a chromosomal breakage syndrome. In contrast, Fanconi anemia, Bloom syndrome, and ataxia-telangiectasia are classic disorders associated with genomic instability and increased chromosomal breakage. Fanconi anemia involves defective DNA interstrand cross-link repair, Bloom syndrome involves defective DNA helicase function, and ataxia-telangiectasia results from defective ATM-mediated DNA damage response. These disorders carry an increased risk of malignancy because of impaired DNA repair.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Chromosomal breakage syndromes → Fanconi anemia, Bloom syndrome, ataxia-telangiectasia

  • Fanconi anemia → DNA cross-link repair defect

  • Bloom syndrome → BLM helicase defect

  • Ataxia-telangiectasia → ATM defect

  • Ehlers–Danlos → collagen/connective-tissue disorder

Exam Pearl:
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome is not a chromosomal breakage syndrome.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯১) Which one is called perineal membrane?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The perineal membrane is the modern anatomical term for the inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm. It is a strong fascial sheet forming the inferior boundary of the deep perineal pouch and attaches laterally to the ischiopubic rami. It provides support to structures in the urogenital triangle and serves as an attachment site for several perineal muscles. Colles fascia is the membranous layer of superficial perineal fascia, while Scarpa’s fascia is the membranous layer of superficial fascia of the lower anterior abdominal wall. The pelvic diaphragm has its own fascial coverings and should not be confused with the perineal membrane.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Perineal membrane = inferior fascia of urogenital diaphragm

  • Colles fascia → superficial perineal fascia

  • Scarpa fascia → lower anterior abdominal wall

  • Perineal membrane → supports deep perineal structures

  • Located in the urogenital triangle

Exam Pearl:
Perineal membrane = inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯২) Bone infarcts are seen in.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Bone infarcts (bone marrow infarction) are a classic complication of sickle cell anemia. In sickle cell disease, deoxygenated HbS polymerizes, causing RBC sickling and microvascular occlusion. This produces ischemia and infarction of bone and bone marrow, which can cause severe bone pain and, chronically, complications such as avascular necrosis of the femoral head. The other anemias listed do not characteristically cause bone infarction.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sickle cell anemia → bone infarction

  • Mechanism → vaso-occlusion

  • Important complication → avascular necrosis

  • Common site → femoral head

  • HbS polymerization → sickling → vascular obstruction

Exam Pearl:
Bone infarcts + anemia = think sickle cell disease.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৩) Which bone is in exception to the law of ossification?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The ulna is the classic exception to the general law of ossification. The usual law states that in a long bone, the epiphysis that appears first is the last to fuse with the shaft. In the ulna, this relationship is reversed: the lower (distal) epiphysis appears first but fuses first, while the upper epiphysis fuses later. This makes the ulna an important anatomical exception frequently tested in medical entrance and postgraduate examinations.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ulna → exception to law of ossification

  • Distal epiphysis of ulna → appears first

  • Distal epiphysis → also fuses first

  • Remember: “Ulna is unusual.”

Exam Pearl:
Ulna = classic exception to the law of ossification.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৪) Spur cell anemia is caused by....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Spur cell anemia is a severe acquired hemolytic anemia seen mainly in advanced chronic liver disease, especially decompensated cirrhosis. Abnormal lipid metabolism in severe liver dysfunction causes excess cholesterol incorporation into the RBC membrane, producing acanthocytes (spur cells). These rigid, irregularly spiculated RBCs are rapidly removed by the spleen, causing hemolytic anemia. It is associated with poor prognosis in advanced liver disease.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Spur cell anemia → chronic liver disease

  • Spur cells = acanthocytes

  • Mechanism → abnormal RBC membrane lipid composition

  • Common setting → advanced cirrhosis

  • Acanthocytes → irregular, uneven projections

Exam Pearl:
Spur cell anemia = acanthocytes + advanced liver disease.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৫) Which muscle is partially attached to articular disc of TMJ?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The lateral pterygoid muscle is partially attached to the articular disc of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Its superior head attaches to the anterior aspect of the articular disc and joint capsule, while its inferior head attaches to the neck of the mandible. Contraction of the lateral pterygoid helps produce protrusion and depression of the mandible and assists in controlling movement of the articular disc during jaw movements. The temporalis, medial pterygoid, and masseter do not have this characteristic attachment to the TMJ articular disc.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Lateral pterygoid → articular disc + capsule of TMJ

  • Superior head → disc/capsule

  • Inferior head → neck of mandible

  • Main action → protrusion of mandible

  • Bilateral contraction → protrusion

  • Unilateral contraction → deviation of mandible to the opposite side

Exam Pearl:
Lateral pterygoid is the key muscle attached to the TMJ articular disc.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৬) Hemochromatosis affects all of the following organs except....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hemochromatosis causes excessive iron deposition in multiple organs. The major affected organs include the liver (cirrhosis), pancreas (diabetes mellitus due to pancreatic damage), and heart (cardiomyopathy and arrhythmias). Iron can also deposit in the skin, joints, and pituitary gland. The salivary glands are not a typical major target organ of systemic iron overload, making them the best answer for the exception.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hemochromatosis → iron overload

  • Liver → cirrhosis

  • Pancreas → diabetes mellitus

  • Heart → cardiomyopathy

  • Skin → bronze/gray pigmentation

  • Pituitary → hypogonadism

Exam Pearl:
“Bronze diabetes” = hemochromatosis → liver + pancreas + heart.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৭) The coronal & sagittal sutures meet at......?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The coronal and sagittal sutures meet at the bregma. Bregma is the landmark where the frontal bone meets the two parietal bones, corresponding to the site of the anterior fontanelle in infants. The lambda is where the sagittal and lambdoid sutures meet. The asterion is the meeting point of the lambdoid, occipitomastoid, and parietomastoid sutures. The pterion is the junction of the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Coronal + sagittal → Bregma

  • Sagittal + lambdoid → Lambda

  • Lambdoid + parietomastoid + occipitomastoid → Asterion

  • Frontal + parietal + temporal + sphenoid → Pterion

Exam Pearl:
Bregma = coronal + sagittal sutures.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৮) Pure red cell aplasia is associated with.....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) is classically associated with thymoma. It is characterized by severe reduction or absence of erythroid precursors in the bone marrow, resulting in profound anemia with normal or near-normal white blood cells and platelets. In thymoma-associated PRCA, an autoimmune mechanism involving suppression of erythroid precursor cells is thought to occur. Other causes include parvovirus B19 infection, autoimmune diseases, and certain drugs. Although PRCA can rarely occur with lymphoid malignancies, thymoma is the classic association tested in MCQs.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PRCA ↔ Thymoma

  • Bone marrow → markedly reduced erythroid precursors

  • WBC → usually normal

  • Platelets → usually normal

  • Acquired PRCA → consider thymoma, parvovirus B19, drugs

Exam Pearl:
Adult with pure red cell aplasia → always look for a thymoma.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৯) Contents of carotid sheath excludes....?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The carotid sheath contains the common carotid artery, internal carotid artery, internal jugular vein, and vagus nerve (CN X). The external carotid artery is not contained within the carotid sheath; it lies outside the sheath after branching from the common carotid artery in the carotid triangle.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Carotid sheath → Common carotid artery

  • Carotid sheath → Internal carotid artery

  • Carotid sheath → Internal jugular vein

  • Carotid sheath → Vagus nerve

  • External carotid artery → NOT inside carotid sheath

Exam Pearl:
Carotid sheath contains ICA, not ECA.

Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০০) Which is an antiapoptotic gene?
Final Model Test-08 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Bcl-X, particularly the Bcl-xL isoform, is an anti-apoptotic member of the Bcl-2 family. It inhibits apoptosis by preventing mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and the subsequent release of cytochrome c. In contrast, Bax and Bim are pro-apoptotic proteins. Bcl-2 itself is another major anti-apoptotic protein. Therefore, among the given options, Bcl-X is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anti-apoptotic → Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Mcl-1

  • Pro-apoptotic → Bax, Bak, Bim, Bad

  • Bcl-xL → inhibits mitochondrial apoptosis

  • Bax/Bak → promote mitochondrial membrane permeabilization

  • Bim → pro-apoptotic BH3-only protein

Exam Pearl:
